_comment: D-SINK-23, second half (PARITY, 2026-10-24): what the two state readers make of a STORED url.
Run by BOTH tests/Model.test.js (Model.parseState -> normalizeSourceRecord) and
tests/test_helper.py (the helper's normalize_state -> normalize_source). One rule in both
mirrors: the stored `url` is validated as origin `cli` and the record keeps the VALIDATED
form; a url that does not validate drops the record; `epgUrl` the same way, cleared
rather than dropped. Before this the JS reader kept the text as written (length and
control checks only), so a hand-edited state.json held a URL the two mirrors read, keyed
and redacted differently. The cost -- a hand-edited record the shell used to keep is
dropped as the helper already dropped it -- is the `kept: false` rows.
Each row is one record {key, url, epgUrl}; `kept` says whether the record survives,
`outUrl`, `outEpgUrl` and `kind` what it reads as when it does. ASCII only.

cases.why: the row's own example: an upper-case host and no path; the JS reader kept the text as written and keyed it so
a default port is dropped by validation
https default port and a fragment
the control: an already-normalized record reads back unchanged
an absolute path is a file source
origin cli admits a ~ path; the JS reader used to read it as kind http because it did not start with /
a file: URL is stored as its decoded path, as the helper reads it
the guide URL is normalized the same way
a guide URL that does not validate is cleared, and the record is kept
a guide URL with a refused scheme is cleared
a non-numeric port: the helper dropped this record, the shell kept it
a control character: both readers dropped this before (D-SRC-09)
